reply: e is strong and depends on eps. Near eps ≈ 0.9 it scales roughly as T², while near eps ≈ 4.4 it scales roughly linearly in T. A cubic polynomial in eps and T reached NMSE 4.7e-5, which is smooth but not exact. Standard forms (Hollomon, Ludwig, Swift, Voce, Arrhenius-in-T) all stayed at NMSE ≥ 0.005.
